prompt: You are the test author: write the checks that catch a recent-items buffer keeping one item too many, one dropping the newest instead of the oldest, and one handing out its internal list.
explanation: A bounded buffer only reveals its bugs once it is full, so every useful check here adds more items than the capacity -- and adding exactly capacity + 2 separates "keeps one too many" from "drops the newest" in a single sequence. Creating a capacity of 1 as well is cheap insurance, because off-by-one errors often survive at 3 and die at the smallest legal size. The last bug is invisible to any read-only test: the only way to notice that items() handed back the buffer's own list is to modify the returned list and then look at the buffer again.
hints: Take the factory up on its offer: factory.create(3) for the ordinary case and factory.create(1) for the tightest boundary.
Add four items to a capacity-3 buffer and expect items().toString() to be "[b, c, d]" -- that one line catches both the keeps-too-many bug and the wrong eviction end.
For the snapshot rule, call items(), clear the list you got back, then call items() again and expect the original contents. Keep everything inside a try that returns false from catch (Throwable t).
